selected.rationale: The Fitness Enthusiast matches the activewear category and works out 4+ times a week, aligning with the brand's primary product. Their preference for technical fabrics and performance claims fits a mid-tier activewear brand.

The Sustainability Buyer focuses on environmental footprint and supply chain transparency, which directly connects to the advertiser's core value of using recycled ocean plastic for sustainable activewear.

The Wellness Optimizer has a low price sensitivity and treats her body like a system to optimize, making her an ideal target for a $120 AOV sustainable activewear brand that values health, fitness, and clean living.

The Gen Z Aesthete is highly visual and cares about whether a brand stands for something, which matches the mission-driven nature of an eco-friendly ocean plastic activewear brand targeted at younger demographics.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes time-saving, convenience, and subscriptions, whereas this brand is a one-off apparel purchase rather than a household consumable or meal kit.
The Pet Parent focuses strictly on pet health, food, and supplies, which has no direct overlap with women's activewear.
The Affluent Classic is aged 50-68 and prefers classic apparel, heritage, and understated luxury, which falls outside the target age range of 22 to 40 for this modern activewear brand.
The Convenience-First Millennial looks for instant delivery and quick commerce grocery or meal services, which does not align with a specialized D2C apparel brand.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has high price sensitivity and seeks deep discounts and budget-aware bundles, conflicting with the mid-tier $120 AOV positioning of the brand.
The Gifter is focused on seasonal gift-wrapping and holiday purchases rather than personal wellness and activewear adoption, making them too transient for a brand-focused campaign.
